Topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

Target audience: Undergraduate students in STEM fields

Section: section_1 — Prerequisites: The Language of Vectors

Lecture lines:
A basis defines our coordinate system.
Vectors are displacements, not just numbers.
Coordinates depend on the basis chosen.

Planned animations:
Create two orthogonal unit vectors in #FFFFFF labeled 'i' and 'j'.
Animate a vector 'v' as a linear combination of 'i' and 'j' in #FFFF00.
Highlight the scalar coefficients as the vector coordinates.

Section: section_2 — The Problem: Viewing Space from Different Angles

Lecture lines:
View the same vector from different angles.
Basis B and Basis C are perspectives.
We need a bridge between these views.

Planned animations:
Display a grid with basis 'B' in #00FFFF and 'C' in #FF00FF.
Show a point 'P' and its different coordinate representations.
Emphasize the distance between representation 'P_B' and 'P_C'.

Section: section_3 — Constructing the Transition Matrix

Lecture lines:
Express new basis vectors as old ones.
These become columns of matrix P.
P maps new coordinates to standard.
Grid lines warp to the new basis.
Now we have our transition machine.

Planned animations:
Represent basis 'B' vectors as columns in a matrix 'M' in #FFFF00.
Visualize 'M' transforming the standard basis into basis 'B'.
Flash the matrix columns to link with 'B' basis vectors.

Section: section_4 — The Change of Basis Formula: The Transformation

Lecture lines:
The formula is [v]B = P * [v]C.
P translates coordinates between systems.
P inverse reverses the translation.
Use robots to navigate local frames.
Map local movement to global space.

Planned animations:
Show 'v_C = P * v_B' formula in #FFFFFF with clear labels.
Animate the transition matrix 'P' shifting the space.
Highlight the final coordinate mapping result.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Application

Lecture lines:
We only change our coordinate description.
The vector remains physically unchanged.
Grid lines rotate, labels update accordingly.

Planned animations:
Display a recap of the 'Change of Basis' formula.
Show a brief real-world rotation coordinate shift in 2D.
Fade out with the key takeaway: 'Perspective changes'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
